title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
why_read: An interesting empirical study of whether capable LLM agents can autonomously devise their own self-improvement strategies without explicit instructions.
analysis: The researchers give an LLM agent a compute budget, tools to gather experience, and a general goal, then observe whether it invents its own learning algorithm using gameplay as a testbed. They find capable models do self-improve, developing strategies that resemble known cognitive learning frameworks and self-generated curricula from ML literature. They also test whether learned text-based strategies transfer to other games and tasks, which is the more practically interesting finding. This touches on real questions about autonomous agent design and the limits of current self-improvement methods, relevant to anyone building agentic AI systems.
